newsitem.title: JORDAN: Bank of Jordan, Jordan-Kuwait revive merger plan.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Jordan, Jordan-Kuwait revive merger plan.

text.p: Two Jordanian banks, Bank of Jordan and the smaller Jordan-Kuwait Bank, have revived a shelved merger plan, banking sources said on Tuesday.

Bankers said the boards of the two banks have revived plans for a merger which go back three years when they agreed the idea on principle. The move fell through apparently over insufficient Central Bank incentives, they said.

But new benefits offered by the Central Bank to encourage mergers, part of a programme to help create a stronger banking system, have prompted the two banks to think again. Bank of Jordan's stake of around 10 percent in Jordan Kuwait Bank could also facilitates the merger, bankers said.

Along with two other banks, Arab Bank and Cairo Amman Bank, Bank of Jordan has captured a major share of Palestinian banking business in the last two years as Jordanian banks rushed to resume operations suspended after Israel's occupation of the West Bank in 1967.

Bank of Jordan posted 1996 net profits of 5.07 million dinars ($7.2 million) against 2.99 million dinars ($4.2 million) in 1995. Its assets stood at 534 million dinars against 457 million dinars in 1995.
